answer: The network can score each identity by the entropy of its action timing: honest agents act irregularly, like waves through a narrow inlet, while a bot fleet fires on a rigid clock. Low-entropy identities face escalating proof-of-work challenges before each trade, and the summit of trust is reserved for high-entropy histories. A hollow schedule of perfectly timed trades betrays a thousand puppets at once, so the farmer must desynchronize every fake, breaking coordination and slowing the attack, while one honest agent passes by simply being irregular.
